note: Jerome has “Much food is in the new fields of fathers; / and others are gathered without judgment.” The second half may have been inspired by Jewish exegesis, see Cyrus H. Gordon: Rabbinic Exegesis in the Vulgate of Proverbs. _Journal of Biblical Literature_ 49 (1930) 384–416, at p. 390. Today, the Hebrew is understood differently, hence the NVg version: _Multi cibi in novalibus pauperum, et est qui perit, deficiente iudicio_ – much food is in the new fields of the poor, and there is one who perishes for lack of judgment.
